$schema_note: Phase 0 proof-of-concept dataset for the billionaire-government-money profile (docs/ideas/billionaire-subsidy-tracker.md). Subject is a named living person: every figure is source-linked. The unit of truth is the COMPANY and the AWARD; the person is a lens. IMPORTANT: the person-to-money link is WEAKER here than for Musk. Thiel is Palantir's co-founder, chairman, and a large shareholder, but he is NOT the CEO/operator (Alex Karp is CEO) — and the Founders Fund items are minority INVESTOR exposure, not control. Money TYPE values: FEDERAL_CONTRACT, FEDERAL_GRANT, FEDERAL_LOAN, TAX_CREDIT_SUBSIDY, STATE_LOCAL_SUBSIDY, REGULATORY_CREDIT. POLITICAL_SPENDING is money flowing OUT from Thiel, tracked here for the side-by-side, and is NOT government money received. NOTE: Palantir government revenue is the company SELLING software/services under contract — that is the government BUYING things, not a subsidy.
subject: Peter Thiel

headline.label: $1.86 billion in U.S.-government revenue in FY2025 (Palantir)
headline.description: Palantir Technologies' U.S.-government segment revenue for fiscal year 2025 was $1.855 billion (+55% year over year), per Palantir's Q4/FY2025 earnings release. Palantir — co-founded and chaired by Peter Thiel — derives the majority of its revenue from government customers (US Army, DoD/Project Maven, the intelligence community, ICE/DHS, CDC/HHS, IRS). There is no Washington-Post-style single 'X dollars to Thiel' total; the cleanest defensible anchor is Palantir's audited/reported U.S.-government revenue, which we present here as the headline. This is REVENUE Palantir earned selling software and services under contract — the government BUYING a product — not a subsidy or a transfer to Thiel personally.
headline.composition: FY2025 U.S.-government segment revenue of $1.855B. Across recent years: U.S.-government revenue was $516M (2022), $732M (2023), $1,121M (2024), $1,855M (2025); total government revenue (US + international) was $723M (2022), $1,036M (2023), $1,468M (2024). Government has been ~55-71% of total company revenue, falling to ~54% in 2025 only because commercial revenue surged.
headline.time_period: FY2025 (fiscal year ended Dec 31, 2025); multi-year series 2022-2025
caveats: This is COMPANY REVENUE FROM CONTRACTS, not a subsidy and not money to Thiel personally. The government is buying software/analytics; Palantir delivers a service and is paid for it. Do not equate it with the Musk-style 'government funding' headline (which mixed contracts, subsidies, loans, and credits).

Person-attribution to Thiel is WEAKER than for Musk. Thiel co-founded Palantir, chairs its board, and is one of its largest individual shareholders (~4-5% of shares; holds founder supervoting Class F stock), but he is NOT the CEO/operator — Alex Karp runs the company. The revenue accrues to a public company owned by many shareholders, not to Thiel's checking account.
FY2025 figure is from the earnings release; the FY2025 10-K was not yet filed at compile time. FY2022-2024 figures are from the audited FY2024 10-K three-year comparative.
Gross revenue is not profit and is not Thiel's personal income. Most of the revenue is spent delivering the work (payroll, infrastructure, R&D).

caveats:
CRITICAL DISTINCTIONS (read before citing any number):

1. PALANTIR GOVERNMENT REVENUE IS A CONTRACT, NOT A SUBSIDY. The headline ($1.86B U.S.-government revenue in FY2025) and the per-year revenue lines are money Palantir EARNED selling software and analytics to government customers. The government is BUYING a product/service at a negotiated price; Palantir delivers it. This is categorically different from the Musk dataset's blend of subsidies, tax breaks, loans, and regulatory credits. Do not describe Palantir's government revenue as 'subsidies' or 'government funding handed to' the company — it is procurement revenue for services rendered.

2. ATTRIBUTING COMPANY MONEY TO THIEL IS WEAKER THAN FOR MUSK — STATE THIS PLAINLY. This is the single most important caveat. Elon Musk is founder + controlling shareholder + CEO/operator of his companies. Peter Thiel is Palantir's co-founder, board chairman, and one of its largest individual shareholders (~4-5%, with founder supervoting Class F stock) — but he is NOT the CEO and does not run day-to-day operations. Alex Karp is CEO and the operating force. So while it is fair to say Thiel co-founded, chairs, and holds a large stake in a company that earns billions from government, the control/operator link is materially weaker than 'Musk got X.' Palantir is a public company whose revenue accrues to many shareholders, employees, and operations — not to Thiel's personal account. Frame every Palantir figure as 'Palantir's revenue,' with Thiel as founder/chair/large-shareholder lens, never as a payment to Thiel.

3. FOUNDERS FUND HOLDINGS ARE INVESTOR EXPOSURE, NOT CONTROL. The Anduril and SpaceX line items are INDIRECT: Thiel co-founded Founders Fund, which is a minority financial INVESTOR in those companies. He is not the founder, CEO, or operator of either (Palmer Luckey runs Anduril; Elon Musk runs SpaceX). Anduril's and SpaceX's government contracts must NOT be attributed to Thiel personally. The SpaceX entry deliberately carries amount=null — its ~$22B+ in government contracts belong to the Musk profile, not this one; only the fact of an early minority stake is recorded. Confidence on all person-attribution for these is LOW.

4. GROSS REVENUE != PROFIT != THIEL'S PERSONAL INCOME. Palantir's government revenue is gross top-line revenue. Most of it is consumed delivering the work (engineering, payroll, infrastructure, R&D). It is not profit, and it is certainly not income that reaches Thiel personally. Any framing that implies the figures landed in Thiel's bank account is false.

5. CEILINGS != OBLIGATED != PAID. Several big Palantir and Anduril numbers are award CEILINGS or contract VEHICLES ('up to'), not money obligated or paid: the $10B Army Enterprise Service Agreement (a 10-year ordering vehicle), the up-to-$22B IVAS and $20B Army counter-UAS vehicles at Anduril. The cumulative ~$1.9B Palantir figure is obligated-to-date and is a different, much smaller basis. Do not conflate ceilings with cash. Do not sum a ceiling and an obligated figure.

6. AGGREGATES CONTAIN THEIR LINE ITEMS — DO NOT DOUBLE-COUNT. The per-year revenue lines are NOT additive into a meaningful 'total' without care (they are annual snapshots, and the cumulative-obligations line and the revenue lines measure different things). The 2022 cycle ~$35M political total CONTAINS the Vance ($15M) and Masters (~$13.5M) items. The 2025-2026 political line is itself a sum of three items. Naively summing the JSON 'amount' fields will over-count and mix incompatible bases (annual revenue, cumulative obligations, contract ceilings, and political spending). Use the headline (FY2025 U.S.-government revenue) or a clearly-labeled per-type breakdown, not a sum of all rows.

7. POLITICAL SPENDING IS MONEY OUT, NOT MONEY IN. The 2016 / 2022 / 2024 / 2025-2026 figures are money Thiel SPENT on politics (a major conservative megadonor — ~$35M in 2022 alone, the bulk behind JD Vance and Blake Masters), included for the side-by-side contrast (public money flowing to companies he founded/invests in, vs political influence he purchased). They are NOT government money received and must never be added to the Palantir revenue figures. Note also the $3M California Business Roundtable item is state ballot-measure spending, not a federal contribution. Thiel's ~$10M Gawker litigation funding is legal spending, not political giving, and is excluded.

8. SOURCING GAPS TO CLOSE BEFORE A PUBLIC LAUNCH. (a) The FY2025 figure is from the earnings release; confirm against the FY2025 10-K when filed. (b) USAspending.gov is a JS app that could not be machine-fetched; the ~$1.9B cumulative and per-agency splits come from aggregators citing it — verify in-browser. (c) The IRS >$113M/>$130M figures are Congressional/press citations of USAspending; confirm the exact award. (d) The Saving Arizona/Masters amount is a range ($13.5M-$15M) and the 2024 ~$1.7M figure should be re-checked against OpenSecrets donor-detail (Thiel ID U0000004022).
